title: Minimax Detection of Treatment-Effect Heterogeneity with Rough Nuisances in Observational Data
banked_reason: D0.5 kernel_substituted: accepted all-dimension frontier and critical limit experiments remain open; upper theorem also has unresolved resolution compatibility
gap_reasons: a real, usable subfrontier, not the promised full kernel

The selected dyadic dimensions do not establish the common regular-refinement and polynomial-degree compatibility required by prop:corrected-moment-bounds; hence its K^{-s/d} null-bias bound cannot yet be instantiated at (M^dagger,K^dagger).
proof_attempt_summary: D0 constructed a candidate matched heterogeneity-detection rate for d <= 4 gamma, including the boundary and all beta values in that regime, using a split corrected-moment test and an observed-law mixture lower bound. The accepted topic required every dimension and critical local experiments; both remain open, so the D0.5 panel found kernel substitution below the field floor. The math referee also found that the selected resolutions do not establish the compatibility premise needed for the upper theorem's bias bound.
tldr: The project now proves the matched observational minimax radius \(r_n^\dagger=\max\{n^{-2\gamma/(4\gamma+d)},n^{-1/(1+d/(2(\alpha+\beta))+d/(4\gamma))}\}\) for every fixed tuple with \(d\le4\gamma\), without a global restriction on \(\beta\). The explicit split corrected-moment test uses a deterministic threshold, and a legal uniform-design two-scale prior proves the all-test converse. At \(d=4\gamma\), the pair activity is bounded rather than vanishing and is controlled by the same fixed amplitude as the two-pair activity. The remaining rate problem is \(d>4\gamma\); multiplier validity and critical local laws remain separate open questions.
gap: Published CATE work separately supplies pointwise minimax estimation, homogeneity-test validity, and regular local power, but not a matched rough-Hölder observational detection radius for distance from an unknown constant with the unknown-propensity and supplied-propensity experiments kept distinct.
fill: An explicitly split profiled quadratic statistic with fully specified constrained training pilots and an exact common-index Rademacher critical value supplies the observational upper bound, smooth full-data causal priors with occupancy-matched observed Bernoulli mixtures supply the all-test converse, and a separately defined fixed-propensity oracle radius supplies only the valid benchmark comparison.
